title: Compatible derived evaluations lift to a strict derived tower map
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of rings. Set $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with levelwise exactness. Derived categories are [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $X,Y\in D(\mathcal B)$, write $X_n,Y_n$ for their derived evaluations and $t^X_n:X_{n+1}\to X_n$, $t^Y_n:Y_{n+1}\to Y_n$ for their transitions. Every family $f_n:X_n\to Y_n$ in $D(\mathcal A)$ satisfying $t^Y_nf_{n+1}=f_nt^X_n$ admits a lift $f:X\to Y$ in $D(\mathcal B)$ whose derived evaluations are the $f_n$. A lift is an isomorphism if every $f_n$ is an isomorphism. Neither uniqueness of the lift nor a functorial choice of lifts is asserted.

source.place: Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck), K-injective resolutions with injective terms; derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective). Agent homotopy-correction proof written in report.md; More on Algebra Tag 091I only lifts objects and is NOT cited as a theorem on morphisms.

proof.text: Choose strict tower complexes $P,V$ and isomorphisms $QP\simeq X$, $QV\simeq Y$, using the complex localization description of the derived category. The index category $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ is small in the stated universe, so the small-module-diagram theorem makes $\mathcal B$ Grothendieck abelian. Apply the injective-term K-injective resolution theorem in $\mathcal B$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $v:V\to J$, with $J$ K-injective and each $J^q$ injective as a TOWER object. Fix the resulting identification $QJ\simeq Y$. Evaluation is exact by the levelwise-abelian theorem, so $v_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Transport the given $f_n$ to maps $\bar f_n:QP_n\to QJ_n$; naturality of $v$ and of the evaluated identifications gives $Q(t^J_n)\bar f_{n+1}=\bar f_n Q(t^P_n)$.

source.place: Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck; application to the small tower category

proof.text: For an object $M$ and positive integer $n$, define $L_n(M)$ to have value $M$ at indices $m\leq n$, zero at $m>n$, identity transitions within its support and zero transitions elsewhere. For an injective tower $T$, the componentwise identity/zero inclusion $L_n(T_n)\hookrightarrow L_{n+1}(T_n)$ is monic by levelwise monomorphisms. Define $a:L_n(T_n)\to T$ by the composite transition $T_n\to T_m$ at $m\leq n$ and zero otherwise. Injectivity extends $a$ to $b:L_{n+1}(T_n)\to T$. Its components satisfy $b_n=\mathrm{id}_{T_n}$ and $t^T_n b_{n+1}=b_n$, so $b_{n+1}$ is a section of $t^T_n$. Apply this to $T=J^q$ and choose sections $s_n^q:J_n^q\to J_{n+1}^q$ in every degree. These sections are graded maps only; no commutation with differentials is needed.

source.place: Tag 079P injective-term clause; elementary extension argument from injectivity

proof.text: Evaluation of the K-injective tower complex $J$ is K-injective by the evaluation theorem (reindex positive integers by $n\mapsto n-1$ to use its natural-number indexing). Therefore the Hom-to-derived-Hom bijection supplies a chain map $a_n:P_n\to J_n$ representing each $\bar f_n$. That bijection is also injective: two chain maps into $J_n$ that represent the same derived morphism have the same homotopy class. Thus an adjacent commutation defect is null-homotopic, rather than merely zero after localization.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, clause (3); existing evaluation-preserves-K-injectives theorem

proof.text: Construct $b_n:P_n\to J_n$ inductively, with $b_n$ homotopic to $a_n$ and $t^J_i b_{i+1}=b_i t^P_i$ for $i<n$. Set $b_1=a_1$. Given $b_1,\ldots,b_n$, compatibility and the Hom bijection show that $D_n=t^J_n a_{n+1}-b_n t^P_n$ is null-homotopic. Choose $H^q:P_{n+1}^q\to J_n^{q-1}$ with $D_n^q=d_{J_n}^{q-1}H^q+H^{q+1}d_{P_{n+1}}^q$, and set $\widetilde H^q=s_n^{q-1}H^q$. Define $b_{n+1}^q=a_{n+1}^q-d_{J_{n+1}}^{q-1}\widetilde H^q-\widetilde H^{q+1}d_{P_{n+1}}^q$. The correction $d\widetilde H+\widetilde H d$ is a chain map, since both products with a differential equal $d\widetilde H d$ after $d^2=0$. It is null-homotopic, so $b_{n+1}$ still represents $\bar f_{n+1}$. As $t^J_n$ is a chain map and $t^J_n\widetilde H=H$, applying $t^J_n$ to the correction gives $dH+Hd=D_n$; hence $t^J_n b_{n+1}=b_n t^P_n$. Previous $b_i$ are unchanged. Recursion over the positive integers now gives all components.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective; agent sequential homotopy correction written out here

proof.text: The adjacent equalities imply commutation with each longer transition by repeated composition. Thus the family $(b_n)$ is a strict tower chain map $b:P\to J$: its degreewise components are natural transformations, and the chain equation is checked at each index. Localize $b$ and compose with the fixed identifications $QP\simeq X$ and $QJ\simeq Y$ to obtain $f:X\to Y$. Its evaluation at $n$ is $f_n$ because $b_n$ is homotopic to $a_n$ and localization factors through the homotopy category. The homotopies between $b_n$ and $a_n$ need not form a tower homotopy; only their evaluation classes are asserted. The choices in this construction give existence only.

source.place: Tag 05RU derived-category localization; agent assembly of the corrected maps

proof.text: Finally let $g:X\to Y$ be ANY lift with all $g_n$ invertible. The Hom bijection in $\mathcal B$, with K-injective target $J$, represents the transported $g$ by a strict tower chain map $c:P\to J$. For every $q,n$, the map $H^q(c_n)$ is invertible, since cohomology factors through localization and the evaluated derived map is $g_n$. Evaluation computes kernels and cokernels levelwise, so $H^q(c)$ is the natural transformation with components $H^q(c_n)$. Its component inverses form a natural transformation: invert the naturality equation on both sides. Hence $H^q(c)$ is invertible for every $q$, making $c$ a quasi-isomorphism by definition. Localization inverts $c$, so $g$ is an isomorphism. This proves the isomorphism clause for every lift, without asserting uniqueness or a functorial choice.
